decision: Do not replace the existing cutting solver.
scope: An experimental streaming exact chance enumerator traverses non-damage prefixes and uses the native endpoint-merging algorithm on conditioned damage suffixes. Prefix mass restores conditional probabilities. Completed disjoint mass is retained on early stop or cap exhaustion, while all unvisited mass remains [0,1]. The witness propagates required lower values into descendants. Static evaluation affects only child order. The full proof run audits every executed chance cell against complete native enumeration: committed raw-state mass must be a subset of the full kernel and committed plus pending mass must be one. Original rational backup, policy, controller, mixture and ceiling checks are reused through a schema adapter. Numeric root values and schedules match the unmerged proof exactly, with two repetitions per backend. Unit checks exercise 324 combinations of move pairs, ordering, caps and stopping points; 12 complete streams equal native kernels. Tests do not establish arbitrary-state equivalence. The same 2200-model finite family and prescribed policy templates are used, not all hidden stats or strategies. Runtime excludes input loading, model replay and the separate chance audits. The experiment has not shown a useful overall speed gain and increases engine executions; retain the previous solver. No deployed-strength claim.
